observations: The runtime supplied no subagent/task identity, so task is null. I opened page-06.png with Read and looked at it.
06-1: the balloon 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' is at top-left with its tail to Meera's head. Her pointing hand, Ravi's phone and Ravi's face are clear.

06-2: the balloon 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' has its tail to Ravi. The phone screen icons are uncovered. The 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients' callout is at the lower left over the monitor and plant. Its right edge stops at the base of the fingers holding the phone's left side, and it does not cover the phone or the thumb on the screen.
06-3: the balloon 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' has its tail down to Meera's head. Her gesturing hand and Ravi's phone at right are clear.
06-4: the caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' crosses the top of the doorway and awning only. Ravi's face and wave, and Ananya and Meera waving, are clear.
The callout is a product label like those on page 02, not text on the phone screen. It covers no screen content.
Natural scan: Meera's statement, then Ravi's question with the callout below it, then Meera's answer, then the closing caption. This is the script order.
Ravi's question (06-2) is answered by 'That's the idea' (06-3) in the adjacent panel. The callout sits at the bottom of 06-2 and does not interrupt the question-answer pair.

transitions.observation: From the consultation room to the reception desk after the consultation. Ravi has his bag and phone, and Meera is at her monitor.
Close on Ravi holding the same dark phone, now showing app cards.
Reverse shot onto Meera answering across the desk. Ravi's phone is visible at the right edge.
Exterior: Ravi leaves waving, and Ananya and Meera wave from the door. The caption closes the visit.
Ravi leaving the clinic cuts to Ravi on a train. The caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' marks the hypothetical move forward in time, as the source requires.

readingReview.comparison: The first reading's order and speakers match the script exactly. Note (a), the callout near Ravi's hand: on inspection it stops at the base of his fingers and does not hide the phone, its screen or the tapping thumb. It is a product callout, not a screen label, so it is not a defect; this lettering passed in the six-page version and is unchanged. Note (b), no caption for the change of place, follows the source. Note (c), the caption over the doorway, covers no face. Nothing unresolved remains.
